applied.problem: Each phase is worked in per unit, so multiplying by the 440 V line base gives E as a line-to-line figure, not the phase voltage (about 422 V); "read E in volts" invites reading 730 V as the voltage in one phase.
"A generator’s drop is bigger than its output" is too absolute: it holds only near full load with a large Xs; at light load or small Xs the drop is smaller than V, yet the triangle is still needed.
